terms.meaning: a fixed label on an element that automated tests use to find it
a reusable piece of the screen that receives values and draws itself

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the control panel
sections.what: Brings in play, pause and refresh icons, a shared panel, the time-ago helper, the Opportunity Map state type, the chip style helper, and a live run feed component.
sections.why: Likely reason: the panel and live feed are shared with other tools.
sections.watch_out: The live feed comes from another tool's folder, so changes there also change this page.

sections.name: FilterRow
sections.title: Row of filter buttons
sections.what: Draws one labelled row with an All button and one button per option. Clicking an option selects it, and clicking it again clears it back to All.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user filter by one option at a time, with a clear way back to All.
sections.watch_out: The label is lowercased to build test IDs, so renaming a label changes the IDs that automated tests rely on.

sections.name: ControlPanel (part 1)
sections.title: Research settings and status panel
sections.what: Shows the research queue numbers (queued jobs, running jobs, how often research runs, and how many accounts are tracked). For admins it also lets them pause or resume background research, choose which industries are monitored, set the run interval from 1 to 168 hours, and save those settings. Other users see the same numbers without the controls.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets an admin control background research from the app, while other staff can still see its status. The interval limit keeps runs from being set to nonsense values.
sections.watch_out: Saving all industries sends an empty list, which the app reads as all industries, so industries added later will be included automatically.

sections.name: ControlPanel (part 2)
sections.title: Closing the research panel
sections.what: Closes the research settings panel and the component that holds it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It only closes the structure opened in the previous section.

sections.name: RunsPanel
sections.title: Run history table
sections.what: Shows a table of recent research runs with the account or industry, status, what started the run, when it finished or started, how many sources were checked, how many signals were created, and notes. Failed or no-evidence runs show a red message. Each run can open a live evidence feed. Runs can be limited to one account and its linked research identity.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets staff see whether research worked, and if not, why, without reading server logs.
sections.watch_out: A run with no evidence is labelled as a research gap, not as proof that nothing exists. Changing the status names will break the colour and label lookups.

summary: Shared pieces for the Opportunity Map control area. This file holds a row of filter buttons, and the rest of its control panel is not in the packet.
purpose: Gives the map a reusable filter row and the control panel that runs and shows research.
why: Likely reason: filters and run history are reused across the map, so they live in one place.
how: 1. The filter row receives a label, the current value, a setter and a list of options. 2. It draws an All button and one button per option. 3. Clicking the active option clears it back to All.
inputs: For the filter row: a label, the current value (or nothing for All), a function to set the value, and a list of option pairs.
outputs: A row of buttons on screen, and calls that set the chosen filter value.
risks: Test IDs are built from the label, so renaming a label can break automated tests. Only the filter row and the start of the control panel were supplied, so the panel's behaviour is not verified.
debug: If a filter does not change the feed, check the value passed to the setter and the parent that reads it. If a button looks wrong, check the chip styling helper in the ui module.
